verses.text: The LORD spoke to me.

“Go say this where Jerusalem can hear you: ‘The LORD says, “I remember how devoted you were when you were young. You loved me like a new bride and followed me out into the wilderness, where nobody had planted a thing.
Israel was set apart for the LORD, the first pick of his harvest. Anyone who swallowed Israel up would answer for it. Disaster would fall on them,”’ says the LORD.”
Listen to what the LORD has to say, family of Jacob, every family in Israel!
The LORD says, “What did your ancestors ever find wrong with me? They wandered so far from me, chased empty things, and ended up empty themselves.

They never asked, ‘Where’s the LORD who brought us out of Egypt? He took us through the wilderness, through deserts and pits, through drought and deep darkness, through a place nobody traveled and nobody lived.’
I brought you into a land bursting with good things so you could eat what grew there. Then you moved in, dirtied my land, and made my inheritance disgusting.

The priests never asked, ‘Where’s the LORD?’ The people who taught the law didn’t even know me. The rulers went against me too. The prophets spoke for Baal and chased things that could do nothing for them.
“So I’m still taking up my case with you,” says the LORD. “And I’ll take it up with your grandchildren too.
Cross over to the islands of Kittim and look. Send word to Kedar and check carefully. Has anything like this ever happened?
Has a whole nation ever swapped out its gods, even though they aren’t really gods? But my people traded away their glory for something that can’t do a thing for them.
“Heavens, be stunned by this. Tremble in horror. Be utterly devastated,” says the LORD.
“My people did two awful things. They walked away from me, the spring of fresh, flowing water, and carved out their own tanks. Those tanks are cracked and can’t hold water.
Is Israel a slave? Was he born into slavery? Then how did he end up captured?
Young lions roared at him, loud and fierce. They wrecked his land. His cities are burned down, and nobody lives there anymore.
The people of Memphis and Tahpanhes have cracked the top of your head too.
“Didn’t you bring this on yourself? The LORD your God was leading you along, and you walked away from him.
So what are you getting out of going to Egypt to drink from the Shihor? Why head to Assyria to drink from the River?

“Your own evil will teach you a lesson, and the way you’ve turned away will call you out. See how bitter and wrong it is to walk away from the LORD your God and have no fear of me,” says the Lord, GOD of Armies.
“Way back, I broke off your yoke and snapped your chains. But you said, ‘I’m not serving.’ On every high hill and under every leafy tree, you bowed down and sold yourself.
I planted you as a fine vine from pure, reliable seed. How did you turn into the wild, rotten branches of some other vine?
Scrub with lye and pile on the soap. I can still see the stain of what you did,” says the Lord GOD.
“How can you say, ‘I’m clean. I haven’t chased the Baals’? Look at the trail you left in the valley. Face what you’ve done. You’re like a fast young camel zigzagging around,

like a wild donkey at home in the desert, sniffing the wind in her craving. When she’s in heat, who can turn her aside? Whoever wants her won’t have to wear themselves out. When her time comes, they’ll find her.
“Save your feet from going bare and your throat from going dry. But you said, ‘Forget it. I love strangers, and I’m going after them.’
The family of Israel will be as ashamed as a thief caught in the act. That goes for all of them, their kings, princes, priests, and prophets.
They tell a piece of wood, ‘You’re my father,’ and a stone, ‘You gave birth to me.’ They turn their backs on me instead of facing me. Then trouble hits, and suddenly it’s, ‘Get up and save us!’
“So where are those gods you made for yourselves? Let them get up and save you when trouble comes, if they can. Judah, you’ve got as many gods as you’ve got towns.
“Why are you bringing a case against me? Every last one of you has gone against me,” says the LORD.
“I struck your children, but it got nowhere. They wouldn’t take correction. Your own sword tore through your prophets like a ravenous lion.

You people living now, think about what the LORD is saying. Have I been a desert to Israel? Have I been a land wrapped in darkness? Then why do my people say, ‘We’ve broken free. We’re never coming back to you’?
“Does a young woman forget her jewelry, or a bride her wedding clothes? My people have forgotten me for more days than anyone can count.
You sure know how to go looking for love! You’ve even taught wicked women your tricks.
There’s blood on the hem of your clothes, the blood of innocent poor people. You didn’t catch them breaking in. Their blood is there because of everything you’ve been doing.
“Still you say, ‘I’m innocent. He can’t still be angry with me.’ Look, I’ll judge you for saying, ‘I haven’t sinned.’
Why are you running all over the place, always changing course? Egypt will leave you ashamed, just like Assyria did.
You’ll leave there too, with your hands on your head. The LORD has rejected the ones you’re counting on, and you’ll get nowhere with them.”
